source.title: Participatory Resource and Socioeconomic Assessment of Ragay Gulf (Bicol Side), Philippines
source.creditedInstitution: Bicol University Center for Policy Studies and Development
source.access: Official BFAR-hosted PDF downloaded and reviewed locally; official FishCORAL page lists the report.

review.reportScope: The title explicitly limits the assessment to the Bicol side of Ragay Gulf.

householdSurvey.interpretation: Livelihood/capture-fisher household survey, not 219 biological fish occurrence records.

productionTable.scopeNote: The report describes production estimates for 11 municipalities and includes San Pascual, Masbate. The table does not provide a taxon-by-taxon capture station, exact catch date, or coordinates.

review.localityDecision: No Quezon-side municipality or Guinayangan/Hinabaan monitoring locality appears in the household sample table. Keep the Bicol-side report distinct from Quezon-site evidence and De Guzman Fishpond.
review.rightsDecision: No item-specific license or reuse statement was found in the official index page checked or extracted PDF text. Keep the detailed species table and derived rows quarantined pending rights review; do not reproduce its taxa or figures in the app.
review.extractionPolicy: This public review records metadata, scope, and a rights/access decision only. It does not transcribe the species table, ingest occurrence rows, or redistribute the PDF.

limitations: The report is a Bicol-side assessment, not a survey of Quezon-side Ragay Gulf municipalities.
Household interviews and aggregated production estimates are not equivalent to station-resolved species occurrence records.
The production table does not establish item-specific rights to create or redistribute a structured species dataset.
Report-level fishery context does not establish current presence, catchability, fishing access, legality, safety, diet, or bait suitability.
nextAction: Use this report as an access and scope reference only. Continue searching for item-level licensed or independently reusable fish evidence tied to Quezon-side Ragay Gulf and Guinayangan; request explicit permission before extracting or publishing the held table.
